author: sonnet
label: climb-05-01
changes: Reordered into overview, terms, decisions, how it runs (numbered steps), failures, diagram, coverage, open questions, as the skill's layout asks.
Added a Terms section defining session, session ID, idle and absolute limits, attempt row, lockout, load balancer, users table, bcrypt and advisory lock (Q1, Q4, Q5).
Renamed login_failures/failed_at to login_attempts/attempt_at, because the table holds every allowed attempt, and stated that success deletes those rows (Q1).
Explained why login_lockouts exists next to the attempt count, in one paragraph after the login steps (Q2).
Made the login failure row split: DB error before vs after the attempt is recorded, noting the attempt still counts and rotation rolls back whole (Q3).
Stated that all state is in shared Postgres so the load balancer and instance choice do not matter (Q5).
Spelled out the separate DELETE by id_hash when the UPDATE matches zero rows, and the lost form input and /dashboard landing after re-login (Q6).
Added what an active user sees when the 12 hours run out (Q7).
Added two open questions: return-to-page after expiry, and outage errors counting toward lockout.

Merged the separate session-ID, cookie, fixation, indistinguishable-failure and CSRF sections into the numbered login steps and one cookie paragraph; updated the diagram for the rename and the delete by id_hash.
Protected-page heading and a new lead paragraph now say /login and /logout skip the session check, answering whether logout runs the UPDATE and that an expired session is fine for logout.
Step 4 of the protected page: the delete after zero rows is best effort and its failure is ignored; the cookie is still cleared and the reply is still 303 to /login.
Failure table: split the protected-page row into the session-check failure (503, cookie kept) and the cleanup-delete failure (ignored, redirect).

Step 3 of the protected page and the diagram: the 503 case is now explicitly the failure of the UPDATE; the diagram marks the delete as best effort and the logout section as not running the protected-page check.
Logout section: added that zero rows covers an expired or unknown session.
Reordered into overview, terms, decisions, diagram, how it runs, failures, rollout, open questions; the diagram now sits right after summary and terms, with the notes after it.
Added to the overview how the app works today (public pages, two instances, shared Postgres) and the reason for Postgres over Redis.
Added terms: load balancer, users table, bcrypt, advisory lock, attempt row, lockout, and defined session fixation inline.
Merged the cookie details (prefix, no Max-Age, no-store, 303, SameSite) into one section and trimmed repeated wording.
Added the lockout-versus-attempt-rows reason, the reason for releasing the lock before bcrypt, and why logout skips the session check, each in a short clause where it appears.
Spelled out the zero-rows step: the separate best-effort delete, form input lost, landing on /dashboard, and that a failed delete is ignored while a failed UPDATE gives 503.
Cut the requirement coverage table, since the steps already state each rule, and removed repeated explanations of the 12-hour expiry.
Moved the rollout (one migration) into its own short section, apart from how the system runs.
Kept the intent unchanged: no design decisions were altered. Renamed login_failures wording to attempt rows consistently.
